criteria_results.title: §2(a): Restore 'entitlement order' language
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank's deletion and restores “Entitlement Order” terminology in the definition and operative control provisions, including Article 8 treatment if an Account is deemed a securities account.

criteria_results.title: Cover note explains §2(a) entitlement order position
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses the “Entitlement Order” issue, rejects the Bank’s deletion/substitution, and explains that retaining both Article 9 Instructions and Article 8 Entitlement Orders preserves Article 8 control under UCC § 8-106 if an account is characterized as a securities account.

criteria_results.title: §2(b): Address springing exclusive control and reject broad Bank carve-out
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline preserves springing exclusive control upon receipt of an NOEC and expressly rejects unrestricted post-NOEC account operation. It provides that Graycliff’s access and instruction rights cease, no new Depositor Instructions may be accepted, and the Bank must comply exclusively with Pinnacle’s instructions, subject only to a narrow exception for processing items originated and accepted before the NOEC.

criteria_results.title: §3: Reject Bank set-off priority over Secured Party instructions
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects Bank Turn 1's provision making the Bank's set-off, recoupment, lien, and security-interest rights superior to Secured Party instructions. It restores a conflicting-instructions waterfall under which Secured Party instructions and entitlement orders control and prevail, with exclusive compliance after an NOEC.

criteria_results.title: §4: Narrow expanded self-help set-off to direct, liquidated obligations
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s broad set-off right for “any obligation,” including contingent and unmatured obligations. It limits permitted debits to documented account fees, returned items, and direct, matured, liquidated, undisputed obligations arising under the deposit-account agreements, while excluding unrelated credit, derivative, affiliate, and other contingent obligations.

criteria_results.title: §5: Propose 3-business-day NOEC compliance period
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5 expressly rejects the Bank’s five-business-day period and proposes compliance no later than the third business day after receipt and authentication of the NOEC. It does not revert to the original two-business-day period.

criteria_results.title: §6: Reject indemnification coverage for Bank gross negligence
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects Bank Turn 1's indemnification coverage for Bank gross negligence and adds a carve-out excluding losses resulting from the Bank indemnitee's gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or bad faith.

criteria_results.title: §7(a): Reject $50,000 aggregate liability cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the $50,000 aggregate liability cap and deletes Section 7.1 in its entirety without proposing a replacement fixed-dollar cap. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: §7(b): Address mutual consequential/punitive/indirect damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly addresses the mutual consequential-damages waiver in Section 8, accepting it in principle while adding carve-outs for indemnification obligations and direct damages, including misapplied funds. The cover note also explains this position.

criteria_results.title: Cover note confirms position on §7(b) mutual damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses the mutual consequential-damages waiver in item 8. It confirms qualified acceptance of a mutual waiver covering indirect, consequential, incidental, special, punitive, and exemplary damages, provided that direct damages and indemnification obligations are not limited.

criteria_results.title: §8: Reject 90-day lookback; propose full subordination or 180-day lookback
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s 90-day lookback and counterproposes a 180-day lookback, while stating that full subordination remains Pinnacle’s preferred position. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: §9: Reject 30-day unilateral termination; propose 90-day notice with transition rights
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s unilateral 30-day termination right and counter-proposes at least 90 days’ prior written notice, continued performance during the notice period, Secured Party transition and coordination rights, and effectiveness only after Secured Party confirms execution of a replacement ACA.

criteria_results.title: §10: Restore New York governing law
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank's proposed North Carolina governing law and restores New York governing law and New York courts in Section 11 (the governing-law issue corresponding to the criterion).

criteria_results.title: Cover note acknowledges New York governing law is strongly preferred with possible flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly states that New York is the appropriate contractual governing law and that Pinnacle is “pushing for it in this turn,” clearly indicating a strong preference for New York law. The criterion does not require an express flexibility statement where strong preference is stated.

criteria_results.title: §12: Restore no-prior-control-agreement representation
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 12 expressly rejects the Bank's deletion and reinstates representations that no other control agreement exists and that the Bank has received no notice of any lien, claim, or adverse interest other than Pinnacle's lien and the depositor's account-holder rights.

criteria_results.title: §13: Restore successor-bank notification obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13 expressly rejects the Bank’s deletion and reinstates a successor-bank notification obligation, requiring at least 30 days’ prior written notice to the Secured Party of a proposed transfer of the Accounts or other succession event, subject to a limited legal/regulatory exception.

criteria_results.title: §11: Accept annual maintenance fee but negotiate down $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly accepts the $3,500 per-account annual maintenance fee ($10,500 total) and negotiates the one-time legal-fee reimbursement down from $15,000 to reasonable, documented external fees capped at the lesser of $7,500 or actual documented fees.

criteria_results.title: ACA maintains form and substance satisfactory to Administrative Agent
criteria_results.reasoning: The counter-turn preserves enforceable UCC control by restoring both Instruction and Entitlement Order concepts, requiring Bank compliance without further Depositor consent, terminating Depositor instruction rights upon NOEC receipt, and giving Secured Party directions priority. It also rejects unrestricted Bank set-off priority and limits Bank liens and debits, so it does not accept changes that would materially undermine control or perfection.

criteria_results.title: Cover note maintains professional and cordial tone
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note is professional, courteous, and appropriate for inter-counsel negotiations. It opens and closes cordially, explains Pinnacle’s positions in a clear and measured manner, and remains firm on key non-negotiable issues without becoming adversarial, informal, or disrespectful.
